steps: The `<table>` tag is used to create a table in an HTML document.
A table can contain rows, headings, and data cells. The `<tr>` tag creates a row, `<th>` creates a heading cell, and `<td>` creates a data cell.

Example: `
NameAge
Ali14
`
items.finalAnswer: The `<table>` tag creates a table in an HTML document, containing rows and heading or data cells.

steps: The CSS box model describes how the space occupied by an HTML element is calculated.
From the inside out, the four parts are: content, padding, border, and margin.
Content is the text or other material inside the element.
Padding is the space between the content and the border.
Border surrounds the padding and content.
Margin is the outer space between the element's border and other elements.
Example: `div { margin: 10px; border: 2px solid black; padding: 5px; }`
items.finalAnswer: The CSS box model consists of content, padding, border, and margin.

steps: HTML (HyperText Markup Language) provides the structure and content of a web page, such as headings, paragraphs, and images.
CSS (Cascading Style Sheets) controls the appearance and layout of that content, such as colours, fonts, and spacing.
JavaScript adds behaviour and interactivity to a web page, such as responding to a button click or updating content.
In brief, HTML gives a page its structure, CSS its presentation, and JavaScript its behaviour.
items.finalAnswer: HTML structures a web page, CSS styles it, and JavaScript makes it interactive.

steps: Choose a code editor, such as Visual Studio Code or Notepad, to write and edit web files.
Install or use a web browser, such as Google Chrome or Mozilla Firefox, to open and test the pages.
Create a project folder and save files in it, for example `index.html`, `style.css`, and `script.js`.
Write the page structure in the HTML file, its styles in the CSS file, and any required interactivity in the JavaScript file.
Open the HTML file in the browser and check that the page works and displays correctly.
Edit the files and refresh the browser to test changes. A code editor's live preview or developer tools can also help with testing and debugging.
items.finalAnswer: Set up a code editor and browser, create the project files, then write, open, and test the web page.

steps: A CSS selector selects the HTML element or elements to which a style rule is applied.
Element selector: selects elements by tag name. Example: `p { color: blue; }` selects all paragraphs.
ID selector: selects the element with a specified `id`, using `#`. Example: `#title { color: red; }`. An ID should be unique on a page.
Class selector: selects elements with a specified class, using a dot (`.`). Example: `.note { font-size: 18px; }`. A class can be used on several elements.
Universal selector: selects all elements, using `*`. Example: `* { box-sizing: border-box; }`.
Grouping selector: applies the same rules to several selectors, separated by commas. Example: `h1, h2 { color: green; }`.
Descendant selector: selects an element inside another element. Example: `div p { color: gray; }` selects paragraphs inside a `div`.
items.finalAnswer: CSS selectors target elements by tag, ID, class, universal selection, grouping, or their relationship to other elements.

steps: A responsive web page adjusts its layout and content to fit different screen sizes, such as phones, tablets, and computers.
Set the viewport in the HTML `<head>` so the page uses the device's screen width: `<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">`.
Use flexible sizes, such as percentages or `max-width`, instead of fixed widths where appropriate. Example: `img { max-width: 100%; height: auto; }`.
Test the page at different viewport sizes and adjust the styles so the content remains readable and usable.
items.finalAnswer: Create a responsive page with a viewport setting, flexible sizing, and media queries for different screen widths.
